_: THE job dependency map and the DEFAULT daily pipeline of SecurityInsight (#269, #306). Read by PowerShell (engine/_shared/SI-JobFlow.ps1: the pipeline runner in a container job and on a VM, Bootstrap, the VM setup step). The web app keeps the same map in Jobs/JobSchedule.cs (Role().Needs) and Jobs/JobFlow.cs (DefaultStages / StageOf) and a test (JobFlowTests) fails when they differ -- change them together. A key is the Container Apps job name without 'caj-si-'. 'needs' are the jobs whose output this job reads; 'stage' is the stage of the pipeline the job belongs to (collect -> correlate (the CIs, then Risk Analysis on them) -> deliver; a schema-1 flow is migrated by it); 'defaultCron' (UTC) is the job's own timer in schedules mode -- Bootstrap's default, and what leaving the pipeline / switching to schedules gives a job that has no remembered timer; a need that is not installed is ignored. 'defaultPipeline' is what a new install gets: its stages in order, each one step after the other except the steps a stage names in 'withPrevious' (they start together with the step above them; JobFlow.cs DefaultTogether); a job not installed is left out. 'defaultFlow' is the same order flattened (what a schema-1 reader sees). 'manualInFlowMode': not a step, and no timer of its own while the jobs run as a pipeline (the risk trend: Risk Analysis writes the daily trend row itself; the job stays runnable by hand). 'ownSchedule' (the updater, framework UPDATE-1.6): NEVER a step of any pipeline -- it runs on its own daily timer (18:30 in the local time of the install's Azure region -- Danish time, the two UTC ticks 16:30 and 17:30, when the region is not known; the updater ends the tick that is not 18:30 there) in every mode; a switch to the pipeline keeps that timer and gives back one an earlier switch took away; a stored pipeline that still has it as a step loses that step when it is read (said in the log). An update waits while the pipeline runs; the pipeline waits (its requests stay queued) while an update runs. 'config-backup' (#404, framework CONFIG-1.3): the daily configuration backup, never a step -- its own timer (18:00 UTC: after the working day, before the pipeline, never at the nightly update). 'retired' (asset-properties, #412 -- the endpoint, identity and azure profilers publish the full asset metadata themselves): the job does nothing any more -- never a step and no timer; a stored pipeline that still has it as a step loses that step when it is read (said in the log), and a need on it is ignored.
_defaultTime: The pipeline starts at 23:30 in the local time of the install's Azure region, after the nightly update at 23:00 in the same zone, so the night's run is complete by 08:00 (owner 2026-10-15): a new install writes 23:30 with its region's zone (SI_Pipeline_StartTime + SI_Pipeline_TimeZone); defaultStartTime in defaultTimeZone (Danish time) applies only when no start time is set, i.e. when the region is not known -- all year: daylight saving moves the UTC time, never the local one. A start time the customer sets (SI_Pipeline_StartTime) is read in the install's own time zone (SI_Pipeline_TimeZone); with no start time set, the default zone applies whatever SI_Pipeline_TimeZone says. Existing installs on the old shipped 22:00 are moved to 23:30 Danish time once by the update (setup/_shared/SI-NightlySchedule.ps1). A schedule stored before time zones keeps its time as UTC.
_reads: 'reads' (a job): jobs whose output of the SAME day it reads when it is there and does without -- the previous run's -- when it is not (verified in code 2026-10-10: azure's identity-tier overlay XENG_AccessedBy* = Get-SIIdentityTierMap over SI_Identity_Profile_CL; endpoint's MostFrequentUser tier = Get-SIBulkDeviceUserCorrelation + AssetProfileByLogonUser over SI_Identity_Profile_CL). Not a need: a failure skips nothing; a step placed before or together with one it reads is warned about. Two reads always see the run before, by design (a cycle): identity reads endpoint's device tiers (Get-SIEndpointTierMap), azure reads endpoint's VM correlation (EndpointAzureCorrelationCache).
_withPrevious: 'withPrevious' (a stage of defaultPipeline): the steps that start together with the step above them -- neither reads the other's output of the same day (azure and endpoint, after identity). A stored pipeline still on the old one-after-the-other layout gets it as it is read (Update-SIJobFlowDefaultLayout, the JSON's 'defaults' level); one a person changed is never re-laid.
_sideBySide: Layout level 3 (#754): Risk Analysis Summary and Detailed start together after the asset correlation -- neither reads the other's output (verified in code 2026-10-18: separate SQL collections, Log Analytics tables, queues, bucket caches and run keys; the only link is the AI summary's leader snapshot in Consistent mode, which the Detailed run reads just before its mail and which is order-independent by design, #108). 'withPreviousSince' (a stage): the layout level at which a 'withPrevious' step was added -- a stored pipeline still on the default layout of its own level gets the current one when it is read and through the update (setup/_shared/SI-PipelineLayout.ps1); one a person changed is never re-laid. Both Risk Analysis jobs write the database through Write-SIDataJsonRows, which paces each writer on the database's own load (SI-SqlPacing.ps1, #749).
_summaryOff: Layout level 4 (#636, owner 2026-10-19: "i prefer to switch so detailed becomes the engine default and summary is optional" / "i dont see a need for summary in pipeline"): Risk Analysis Summary (risk-analysis) is OFF by default -- 'defaultEnabled': false, the existing per-step on/off switch; a new pipeline has the step, switched off. Every Summary-shaped view is a grouping of the Detailed findings (data-model/summary-groupings.locked.json). A stored pipeline below level 4 that is still the default of its own level with every step on gets the step switched off as it is read and through the update (Update-SIJobFlowDefaultLayout / JobFlow.ConvergeDefaultLayout, setup/_shared/SI-PipelineLayout.ps1); one a person changed keeps it (one line says so). The risk trend and the data sync need Risk Analysis Detailed only. The next release removes the step.
_startsWhenReady: 'startsWhenReady' (a Deliver job, #754): in a run of the whole pipeline the step starts as soon as the steps it reads have ended -- its 'needs' and 'reads' that are placed above it, and every step of Collect -- not after every step above it -- and its 'heldBy': steps it does not read but that hold it by the owner's rule (2026-10-13: a failed Risk Analysis Detailed holds every connector; the CMDB connectors read only the CIs, so they wait for Detailed by that rule, not for data). Risk Analysis Detailed is enough for the vulnerability connector and the CMDB connectors; the data sync reads Risk Analysis Detailed (and stores a Summary collection when the optional Summary step ran) and the vulnerability connector's events. What holds it is judged on those steps and on every step above it that has already ended (a failed Summary that ended before it starts is said in its record, as before): one of them that failed, was held or was skipped holds it as before (nothing goes out on a report it needs that is not whole -- absence is not remediation), with the same exceptions (runsOnStored, runsWithoutNiceToHave). A step without it (the daily mail, the verification service) waits for every step above it. A run of one stage or one step, and an install's first collection (nothing is written to the customer's systems before one run is complete), are not changed. 'required' (#748, the verification service -- it runs the daily data health check, CR2): the update adds it to a stored pipeline that does not have it where its job is installed, and the web app does not remove it (its off switch is SI_DataHealth_Enabled).
_runsOnStored: 'needs' = the job reads the output of those jobs OF THIS RUN: when one of them did not succeed it is held. 'runsOnStored' (a job; read by the PowerShell runner only): the job works on what is STORED and holds back by itself whatever is not complete, so after a step of Correlate (the CI build, Risk Analysis) did not succeed it still runs -- the data sync (it loads only whole collections whose run is shown complete, closes no finding on one that is not, and sends nothing to an output in such a run) and the verification service (it only reads). One failed step then does not cost the customer the rest of the run. NEVER on a job that writes to the customer's systems, changes a ticket or sends a mail: those keep their need. 'brings' (a job): what the job would have brought, as a person reads it -- named in the sentence of a run in which it failed or was held. 'assetBuild' (one job): the build of the merged assets -- on a new install's first collection nothing that rests on it runs before it has finished whole. 'niceToHave' (a job: Risk Analysis Summary -- the overview for management; the owner 2026-10-13: "connectors only need detailed ... summary is nice-to-have") + 'runsWithoutNiceToHave' (a job: the CMDB connectors, the vulnerability connector and its ServiceNow form, the data sync): when the ONLY steps that failed after Collect are nice-to-have ones, a step with this mark runs in full on this run's own result -- the findings (Risk Analysis Detailed) and the merged assets of this run are whole. It stays held when Risk Analysis Detailed or the asset correlation did not succeed, and on an install's first collection. The daily mail has no such mark: it waits for a complete run. Off for the whole install: SI_Pro_Pipeline_GoOnAfterFailedStep = $false.
_title: 'title' (a stage of defaultPipeline): the stage as a heading and in the overview -- its name plus what the stage is for (data-in, data structure, data-out). 'name' stays the short name used inside a sentence about one step, and is what a pipeline stores. The title is decided from the stage id when a pipeline is shown, so a stored pipeline shows it without being rewritten; a name a person gave a stage is kept.

jobs.brings: a part of the asset list (its correlation did not finish)
